source.title: Understanding the Skill Gap in Recurrent Language Models: The Role of the Gather-and-Aggregate Mechanism
source.authors: Aviv Bick; E. Xing; Albert Gu

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies Gather-and-Aggregate retrieval heads, not induction heads or the induction-head claims listed here. It mentions induction heads in related work but does not test, rely on, or argue against the specified claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports extensive experiments on G&A heads and in-context retrieval. Those findings concern a related but distinct mechanism; they do not measure induction-head formation, the training-time phase change, or few-shot learning as specified in the claim versions. The paper also cites prior induction-head work, but reports no results from those cited studies as its own.
record.test_reason: The study identifies and ablates Gather-and-Aggregate retrieval heads in pretrained Transformer, SSM and hybrid models on MMLU, KV-retrieval and other benchmarks. It never identifies induction heads, previous-token composition, training dynamics, or loss-by-token-index in-context learning. Induction heads appear only in related work. The G&A two-stage composition is a related but different circuit (segment summarisation plus argmax-like retrieval), not [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying. Its cross-architecture claim is about G&A heads, not heads with induction behaviour.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that Transformers and SSMs both implement in-context retrieval via a Gather-and-Aggregate mechanism concentrated in a few heads. SSMs implement it less sharply, which localises the Transformer–SSM gap, and hybrids offload aggregation to attention. They also argue MMLU mainly reflects retrieval rather than knowledge, and say G&A's role in in-context learning and copying warrants further study.
record.recipe_differences: The study identifies and ablates G&A heads and tests retrieval across pretrained Transformer, SSM, and hybrid models; it does not reproduce induction-head measurements or training-dynamics experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The KV-Retrieval appendix reports that the final prompt character changes the visibility of head-level retrieval effects: without a trailing space they emerge with 20–30 key-value pairs, while the space-delimited prompt requires longer dictionaries for similar effects.

fits_no_version.finding: Across Llama-3.1-8B, Llamba-8B (Mamba-2), Falcon-Mamba-7B (Mamba-1) and Zamba2 hybrids, a few Gather and Aggregate heads are necessary and sufficient for in-context retrieval on MMLU and KV-retrieval. SSM implementations are smoother and more redundant. Hybrids put aggregation in attention layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context retrieval in pretrained Transformer, SSM and hybrid LMs concentrates in a small two-stage Gather-and-Aggregate head circuit, implemented less sharply in SSMs.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported outcomes. Several claims about G&A concern selected heads and particular retrieval benchmarks; the paper itself says G&A's role in in-context learning and copying warrants further study.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many additional G&A ablation results in Tables 2–5 and Figures 2–10. They are omitted because they concern the same adjacent G&A mechanism rather than any V1–V7 induction-head claim; the rows retained capture representative stated outcomes and model-family coverage.

untested.parts: Previous-token-head composition and the [A][B]…[A]→[B] induction circuit in attention-only transformers.
Training-time formation, abruptness, co-occurrence with in-context-learning gains, and a loss bump.
The share of loss-by-token-index in-context learning attributable to induction heads in large models.
The presence of induction-behaviour heads across families and architectures. Cross-architecture results concern G&A heads only.
Effects of data or training setup on induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Whether few-shot task learning runs through non-induction mechanisms. The authors explicitly leave G&A's role in in-context learning open.
Sub-steps or multiple transitions in induction-head formation.

record.verdict_notes: No result bears on any induction-head version, so no verdicts are given. The record's T6/discusses classification is kept. One could argue the G&A cross-architecture finding loosely parallels V4 universality of retrieval-like heads. However, the heads are not characterised by induction behaviour (prefix matching or copying), so linking them to V4 would be a construct mismatch. There are no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Whether heads compose with a previous-token head or implement the specific [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying circuit.
Induction-head formation over training time, abruptness, its timing relative to in-context-learning gains, and a training-loss bump.
Whether induction heads account for most loss-by-token-index in-context learning in large transformers.
Whether heads with induction behaviour occur across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
How data or training setup affects whether and when induction heads form or whether in-context learning persists.
Whether few-shot task learning is carried mainly by mechanisms other than induction heads.
Whether induction-head formation consists of separate sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Minimal
rows.operation_detail: Retained both identified critical heads, L16H22 and L17H24, while removing other heads in the final two layers; compared with retaining neither.
rows.note: G&A-head result, not a measurement of induction heads.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Minimal
rows.operation_detail: Retained only L17H24 among the identified critical heads in the final two layers; compared with retaining neither.
rows.note: The paper describes the result as near random guessing; G&A-head result, not an induction-head measurement.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B

rows.note: Caption gives this example configuration; result concerns G&A retrieval.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B

rows.subject: Llamba-8B
rows.operation_detail: Retained the identified critical heads in both final layers, removing other heads there; compared with retaining none.
rows.note: The table reports the selected-head configuration and the no-critical-head configuration; G&A-head result.

rows.subject: Falcon-Mamba-7B
rows.operation_detail: Retained four identified critical Mamba-1 channels across the final two layers; compared with retaining none.

conditions.value: L35 channels 3186 and 5143; L36 channels 6607 and 7305

rows.note: The authors report that four channels suffice to recover 52.26% accuracy; G&A-head result.

rows.subject: Zamba2-7B
rows.operation_detail: Disabled nine selected attention heads by zeroing the final row of each head's attention matrix.
rows.note: The paper attributes the drop to disabling aggregation in attention layers.
rows.check: MMLU falls from 64.3% to 34.9%, near the 25% random floor, which the paper calls a 4x drop relative to chance. This is a strong effect, closer to observed than partial, though the row is not linked to any version.

rows.subject: Zamba2-7B
rows.operation_detail: Disabled nine selected attention heads by zeroing the final row of each head's attention matrix.
rows.note: Knowledge-task score is reported as stable while MMLU falls.
rows.check: Stable knowledge-task accuracy (70%) is a control showing the ablation is specific, not an effect of the intervention. No baseline is reported, so the state 'observed' is not meaningful. It should be marked as a control row.

rows.subject: Llamba-8B
rows.operation_detail: Replaced layer 17 with the corresponding Llama-3.1-8B layer, without fine-tuning.
rows.note: The paper links the gain to G&A heads in the replaced layer.

rows.subject: Llamba-8B
rows.operation_detail: Swapped only L17H24 for the corresponding attention head from Llama-3.1-8B, leaving other SSM heads intact.
rows.note: The paper reports this as an additional hybrid experiment.

rows.subject: Llamba-8B
rows.operation_detail: Replaced L17H24 and L17H27 with the corresponding attention heads from Llama-3.1-8B.
rows.note: The paper reports this as an additional hybrid experiment.

rows.subject: Llamba-8B
rows.note: This is one point in the paper's head-ablation sweep.
rows.check: Llamba-8B MMLU falls only from 60.7% to 58.1% (-4.3%) after 30 heads are removed. The paper presents this as gradual degradation and redundancy, so 'absent' or a small effect fits better than partial.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
